\section{Confined solid-iron export: a physical architecture with missing admission}

\subsection{Mechanism and its demonstrated antecedents}

The desired operation reduces iron upstream of a gangue-retaining boundary,
deconstructs admitted metal at a contact, transports atoms through a confined
path and rebuilds/harvests metal downstream. It seeks to avoid melting gangue,
not merely reproduce fine-ore reduction.
\href{https://arxiv.org/html/1302.5709v2}{Coh et al. (2013)} experimentally moved
largely crystalline Fe through smaller CNT constrictions; their surface
reconstruction explanation and possible refining application are prior art.
\href{https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms9071}{Melinte et al. (2015)}
demonstrated export onto graphene and reverse admission of prepared external
nanoparticles. Their interface is nearby, conductive and nanoscale. Carbon
reaction, carbide formation and tube changes prevent treating the wall as
inert. Neither result demonstrates raw-ore extraction or bulk throughput.

A permanently continuous, hot 3 nm Fe shell is not a justified material.
\href{https://www.nature.com/articles/srep46725}{Fe-film dewetting on alumina}
is experimentally used to form catalyst particles. The more credible mutation
is an independently conducting capillary with a confined moving/regrowing Fe
plug. It must repeatedly acquire fresh metal from actual reduced ore, retain
source contact as the domain shrinks, reject impurities, harvest downstream
metal and preserve or restart a transport root. Those are required services,
not consequences of surface diffusivity.

\subsection{Governing model and conditional flux}

For capillary radius $r$, active length $L$, open fraction $f$, surface molar
density $\Gamma_s$, diffusivity $D_s$ and temperature $T$, stipulate
\begin{align}
 \mu&=\mu_0+\gamma V_m\mathcal K+V_m\sigma_h+RT\log a_{\rm Fe},\\
 J_{\rm mol}&=\frac{2f}{r}\frac{D_s\Gamma_s}{RT}
          \left[Z^*F E-\frac{\partial\mu}{\partial x}\right].\label{eq:ironflux}
\end{align}
Here $\mathcal K$ is mean-curvature sum, compression raises $\mu$, $V_m$ is
molar volume, $F$ is Faraday's constant, and $Z^*$ is effective migration
charge. All circumference active, uniform coefficients, connected metal,
open source/sink and no poisoning are assumed.

# Electrical series construction with explicit feed and product interfaces

Date: 2026-10-12. Status: circuit construction and conditional resource bounds; not a demonstrated iron-extraction process. All numerical geometry below is illustrative. Material conductivity, contact resistivity, membrane stability, reduction chemistry, atom supply, and selective transport are not validated here.

## Main result

A high projected current density does **not**, by itself, impose the same enormous current at the power-supply terminals. Equal-area membrane cells can be electrically connected in series while receiving feed and collecting product in parallel. This trades current for voltage at unchanged ideal power.

The escape has three mandatory costs: every local contact still carries the original current density, the feed/product compartments must remain electrically isolated while powered, and the conductors must physically cross or bypass the material-access spaces. A common conducting metal-product collector invalidates the series circuit. A batch bipolar cartridge, de-energized before common collection, is a concrete way to meet isolation. Its required storage gaps expose a substantial conductor-volume/heat tradeoff. It does not solve the acquisition of Fe atoms from ore.

## Stipulated transport law and electrical notation

Take as the hypothetical local membrane contract

    atom flux per projected area = 2 f D_s c_s Z* e E / (r k_B T),
    conducting area fraction g = 2 f t/r,
    projected current density j = sigma_Fe g E,
    local active voltage v = E L.

The analysis assumes the resulting atom flux and j are linear in the same E. It does not establish that contract. Let A be the total active membrane area *online*, and let m be the corresponding iron mass flux per projected area. The root agent owns atom/electron accounting.

## Construction: electrically series, materially parallel

1. Divide active area A into N equal cells of projected area a=A/N.
2. Each cell has an electrically conducting Fe transport membrane between distinct source and destination current collectors. Feed and product chambers have insulating walls and their own ports.

# Matter invention: solid-state iron export across a gangue-retaining boundary

2026-10-12. Status: **a physical architecture candidate, with a demonstrated nanoscale transport antecedent and several decisive unresolved transfer gates. No ore-extraction device, novelty clearance, economic advantage, experiment, or major capability has been established.**

The intended large consequence is iron from fine, 45–60 wt% Fe ores without agglomeration, acid dissolution, or melting the gangue. The candidate operation is to reduce iron at the upstream face of a nanoporous boundary, deconstruct the resulting metal at an admitted contact, transport its surface atoms through a confined path, and rebuild/harvest metal downstream. Gangue stays upstream. The strongest surviving mutation uses independently conducting, confined nanocapillaries and a moving/regrowing solid Fe plug, rather than assuming a permanently continuous 3 nm Fe film.

This is a proposed new ore-handling architecture built around old physical operations. Atomic transport through nanotubes and even the possibility of refining nanoparticles during their reconstruction are explicitly prior art. Novelty of the integrated raw-ore architecture is **UNKNOWN**. The construction has not escaped its atom-admission and electrical/material boundary.
